claim: The edit overlay reads the selection from, and listens on, the global document, so it stops responding when its container is in another document

triage.scenario: a host portals its canvas into an iframe (or a popup window) and passes a `container` there. `onBlur` checks `overlay.ownerDocument.hasFocus()`, but `selectionchange` and the outside `pointerdown` are registered on the global `document`, and `readSelectionOffsets` and `selectOffsets` use the global `window.getSelection()`. The iframe's selection never fires those listeners, and the outer selection is never inside the overlay, so `readSelectionOffsets` is always `null`. No range is ever published, so `applyStyleToSelection` and `toggleStyle` return early: the style shortcuts and chrome do nothing, and a press outside never commits. overlayScroll.ts:108, overlayOpen.ts:33/69 (`document.createRange`, `document.head`) and domOffsets.ts:108 have the same split between the global document and `ownerDocument`.

claim: The `applyStyleToSelection` doc leaves out that taking off a node-level script also needs `setStyle`/`onChange`

The docs say `setStyle` is "needed only to turn underline, strikethrough or overline off", and `applyStyleToSelection` describes the node-rewrite path only for flags, so a host reading them has no reason to expect the script toggle to be declined (or that a commit will call `setStyle` for it).

claim: A CR kept before an LF draws as a space in the overlay, though the comment says it draws nothing

The CR is left in the text node; CSS Text 3 treats U+000D as a space, and under the overlay's `white-space: pre` a trailing preserved space does not hang, so line one is a space wider than on the canvas (which draws the CR as nothing): the right-aligned first line sits one space left of the canvas glyphs, and `max-content` width grows by it. claim: Typing over a selection that starts at a run boundary takes the earlier run's style, but pasting over the same selection takes the first replaced character's style

triage.scenario: runs `[{text:'ab'}, {text:'cd', bold:true}]`, selection [2,4) (the bold "cd"), made by `selectOffsets` or a drag that anchors at the end of "ab"'s text node (`charOffsetToDomPosition(2)` returns `(text "ab", 2)`). Typing "x": `onBeforeInput` returns early for any non-collapsed caret, so the browser deletes the range and inserts into the text node holding the start, giving a plain "x" (the run before). Pasting "x" over the same selection goes through `styledForRange`, which reads `runStyleAt(runs, at.start + 1)`, the first replaced character, giving a bold "x". claim: `commit` / `startEdit` read a stale edit id captured from the render they were made in

An unclipped overlay inherits the container's CSS direction, so direction 'auto' text with no strong character lays out RTL in an RTL page while the canvas lays it out LTR

triage.scenario: host page or container is `dir="rtl"`; a node with `direction: 'auto'`, `align: 'start'` holds digits only, or is empty when an edit opens on it. `applyOverlayDirection` clears `direction` to `''`, so the overlay inherits `rtl` from the container. Under `unicode-bidi: plaintext`, a paragraph with no strong character falls back to that inherited direction, and `text-align: start` follows it, so the caret and text sit at the right edge. The canvas's `paragraphDirection` returns `ltr` for the same text, and `overlayAlignEdge` (canvas side) anchors left. So the overlay and the canvas disagree. `placeScrolled` pins `direction: ltr` on its box, so a clipping node inherits LTR, but `placeLoose`'s `bareBox` sets nothing. The two placements answer the fallback direction differently. It should be `ltr` on both, as the canvas does.

triage.scenario: a node seeded with `"a\r\nb"`. `appendOverlayText` leaves the CR as raw text because an LF follows it (`domRuns.ts:57`), and the module's own comment says the CR then draws nothing. If the user puts the caret at the start of `b` and presses Backspace (deleting the LF), or types a character between the CR and the LF, the DOM holds `"a\rb"` or `"a\rX\nb"`. Each keystroke then runs `resplitSmallCaps` → `normalizeSmallCaps`, which rewrites a stretch only when `piecesMatch` fails. Raw CR text matches its pieces, so the CR never becomes a `<span data-break>`. The canvas treats the lone CR as a hard break (`isHardLineBreak(13)`) and shows two lines; the overlay draws nothing there and shows one, and the caret walks a different layout than the text it stands for. It stays that way until some restyle or paste happens to rewrite the runs. It should be turned into a break stand-in once it is no longer followed by an LF.
triage.cause: stand-ins only written on full rewrites, never re-derived after browser edits
